_doc: Performance budgets for agent-dash. Every number carries its measured baseline on the reference machine and 2x headroom: budget ~= 2x baseline, so a breach means a real regression, not noise. A change that breaks a budget must fix the code or raise the budget here with a written reason (see docs/perf.md). tests/perf/test_perf_budget.py (ADASH_PERF=1; selected by scripts/gate.sh for dash/store/*, dash/server.py, dash/sources/*, dash/phases.py, dash/pricing.py, dash/taskmatch.py, dash/state.py) asserts cold/warm endpoint latency on the 1x and 5x seeds, steady-state CPU, per-source poll duration, and the incremental scaling rule. dash/doctor.py slow-endpoint reads endpoints.*.warm_ms from this file.
reference: MacBook Pro, synthetic seeds from scripts/perf_seed.py (1x: 8,431 runs / 157k usage rows / 244k samples / 70 MB; 5x: 42,155 runs / 787k usage rows / 1.2M samples / 355 MB), warmed server, 2026-10-19/20
headroom_rule: budget is 2x the measured baseline, rounded up; raise only with a written reason
cold_scaling_note: A cold open must touch every row once, so cold endpoints scale linearly with data by construction (measured 3.7-5.7x at 5x; no accidental superlinearity). The sublinear guarantee this gate enforces is the incremental one below: a fixed-size write refolds only its runs, independent of total data. Per-scale cold caps live next to each endpoint.

churn._doc: Live-like churn: a writer lands usage on 5 live runs every 200 ms while tabs poll snapshot+runs (tests/perf/test_perf_budget.py::test_churn_coalescing_under_budget, ~20 s window on the 1x seed). Baselines measured on the reference machine 2026-10-20; budgets keep the 2x headroom rule. recompute_min_interval_s bounds the recompute rate (one per ttl_s, not one per request); hit_ratio_min proves coalescing engages; endpoint_p95_ms is the served p95 under churn; *_cold_p50_ms are recompute costs with the TTL bypassed. Reference baselines: recompute interval ~1.5 s, hit ratio ~0.97, p95 ~40 ms, cold snapshot ~35 ms, runs ~20 ms, concurrency ~20 ms, workstreams ~45 ms on the 1x synthetic seed.

scaling.incremental_note: One fixed-size usage write, then _usage_by_run: 5x data costs under 2.5x the 1x time (measured ~1.0x: only the written run refolds). A linear refold regresses this to ~5x and fails the gate.

cpu_steady_note: process cputime delta over a 20 s window with stub sources polling and one simulated open page (conditional snapshot every 2 s) on the 5x seed
poll_note: every source poll duration under 1 s against small synthetic roots (overhead bound); live-workload poll durations are baselined in docs/perf.md
